operatorProperties.code:
def process(loadIdentityTheftFiles, loadFraudFiles) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    def to_long(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        # Normalize to 2-column table: msa, reports
        cols = list(df.columns)
        msa_col = cols[0]
        reports_col = None
        for c in cols:
            if c.strip() in ["# of Reports", "# of reports", "Number of Reports", "Reports"]:
                reports_col = c
                break
        if reports_col is None:
            # Many files use 'Unnamed: 1' for the count column
            reports_col = "Unnamed: 1" if "Unnamed: 1" in df.columns else cols[1]

        out = df[[msa_col, reports_col]].copy()
        out.columns = ["msa", "reports_raw"]

        # Drop header/footer/noise rows
        out["msa"] = out["msa"].astype(str).str.strip()
        out["reports_raw"] = out["reports_raw"].astype(str).str.strip()
        bad_msa = {
            "nan",
            "Metropolitan Area",
            "Source: Consumer Sentinel Network Data Book 2024, Federal Trade Commission",
            "Source: Consumer Sentinel Network Data Book 2024, Federal Trade Commission.",
            "",
        }
        out = out[~out["msa"].isin(bad_msa)]

        # Coerce numeric reports
        out["reports"] = pd.to_numeric(out["reports_raw"].str.replace(",", "", regex=False), errors="coerce")
        out = out.dropna(subset=["reports"])

        # In case of duplicates across files, sum (shouldn't happen, but safe)
        out = out.groupby("msa", as_index=False)["reports"].sum()
        return out

    idt = to_long(loadIdentityTheftFiles)
    frd = to_long(loadFraudFiles)

    merged = idt.merge(frd, on="msa", how="inner", suffixes=("_identity", "_fraud"))
    merged["identityExceedsFraud"] = merged["reports_identity"] > merged["reports_fraud"]

    any_true = bool(merged["identityExceedsFraud"].any())
    return pd.DataFrame([{ "answer": "Yes" if any_true else "No" }])

operators.customDisplayName: Transform identity theft and fraud CSV concatenations into standardized [msa, reports] tables (use first column as MSA name; use '# of Reports' if present else 'Unnamed: 1' as count; drop header/footer rows; coerce counts to numeric; groupby msa sum reports). Inner-join identity vs fraud on msa; compute whether any MSA has identity reports > fraud reports; output single-row DataFrame with column 'answer' ('Yes'/'No').
